I buy most of my groceries from a shop close to my place. I come to Kirana Ghar only for certain items that are unavailable at that shop.
Kirana Ghar has a really wide variety of items - and for each item there is a choice, e.g. for peanuts there are four types. Prices are OK. customer_updates.name: Suraj Parui
customer_updates.text: Hi I have been going to this supermart for years now and it's been an amazing place throughout. However I did have one bad interaction a few days back. I needed to get a cardboard box for some personal use and I went in to ask if I could buy one of the empty product boxes. The staff were helpful. I found a box and they said ask the cashier if it's possible to buy. I was just about to start talking to the cashier that an (old male) security guard called me over away from the cashier towards the exit (I was away from the exit door, it was he who called me over) I told him I asked the staff and I was going to ask the cashier. He asked me to hand over the empty box and I tell him I was going to show it to the cashier only to ask to buy. He insisted so I gave it to him. Then he says "Give me 10 rs" now let me be very clear. I don't have a problem giving money for the box. It was my plan to do so. But does he think he is the manager that I need to pay HIM money to buy something? I was polite and I explained that I don't have a problem paying as long it's the cashier he raises him voice and takes me over to one staff member who weighs and packs grains and tells him "We sell boxes for 10 rs" as if he's the store manager. He's a damn security guard. And the staff nods along to not make a scene. Again it's not about 10 rs. I come here to buy my groceries and pay 2 to 3 thousand weekly. And I did nothing without asking the nice staff. This was very disappointing and rude behaviour from his guard (especially over 10 rs)

featured_reviews.name: komal jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
Last week I bought black raisins, ate them for three days, and on the fourth day I found out they were FULL of worms. When I emptied the packet onto a plate, it was disgusting — literally filled with worms. Imagine eating that without knowing.
And the worst part? When I went to the shop, the young owner didn’t even have the basic decency to talk to me. He behaved like I was disturbing him and acted as if selling spoiled, worm-infested food was normal. He pushed me off to his staff and refused to take any responsibility. Instead of apologising or fixing the issue, they insulted me by weighing the leftover raisins and offering a tiny refund — like they were doing me a favour. Pathetic.
No sorry, no concern, no accountability. I threw the bill there and told them to keep the money. A store that sells rotten products AND treats customers like they’re asking for charity has no shame. They only care about profit, not about the people who trust them.
Because I was a regular customer, I avoided creating a scene in the crowd and went at closing time thinking about their shop. That was my biggest mistake — I should have exposed them right there in front of all the customers.

featured_reviews.name: Humayunn Peerrzaada
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ramzan ke liye kuch special food items lene the. Crawford Market toh final destination tha hi, lekin is naye Gulf store jo Mazgaon me hai, uske baare mein kaafi suna tha — so we decided to visit.

Cozy little place, stocked with food and drink items mostly available in the Middle East. We were looking for specific drinks like Safa Date Milk Shake, B. Laban’s desserts, Kiri Cream Cheese and other iftar favourites — and found a good variety here.

Prices are slightly on the higher side, but when you’re craving something authentic, there’s always a price to pay. We usually love Safa Date Milk Shake — that wasn’t available, so we picked up Almarai instead. Big brand, good quality, though the taste for us still doesn’t beat Safa.

Overall, a good visit and a satisfying buy — especially just a week before Ramzan. Perfect for picking up special iftar delicacies.

featured_reviews.name: Faisal Qureshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
It was a waste of time and money. Please read full to understand the reason.

My wife saw a vlogger video and decided to visit this store. I drove my wife from Panvel to this store with high expectations. But we were disappointed when we didn’t get those products we were looking for because they were out of stock. Since we had travelled from so long to visit this store we decided to buy some items. So we did and when the biller asked me to pay I was utterly shocked to listen to the price she said. Honestly they overcharged too much. I have few stores in NAVI Mumbai like Ajwa, Ajfan, and some local stores who keep imported items and those are very cheaper than what this store is selling. For example I bought a cola gummies for my kids that I usually buy from my nearby house stores who sells the same imported gummies for 200/- rupees and for the same gummies I paid 300/- rupees in Farm Fresh. This is only one example I can gave, just imagine the price variation for other products. From my experience the products I bought shouldn’t be more than 3,500/- but I paid 5,200/- for them. That’s why I said the products are over prized. I spend so much time and money and got very disappointed.
